agree.reason: The tone is measured and the four asks are specific and cheap to meet, so a manager who thinks the company has handled things well could answer them without losing face; still, nothing pushes her to fund anything beyond paperwork and a meeting.

honest.reason: Every number comes from the brief and the derived figures hold up (41 days is about one in eight by mid-November, and 74 of 112 is two in three); the upper-floor wheelchair scenario is framed as 'can mean', so it stays inside the facts.

works_the_facts.reason: It works the raw facts into stronger forms: one day in eight, two households in three, and the point that eight weeks from June ran out in August, the month of the longest outage.

right_comparison.reason: It shows that doing nothing means the same repeated estimate while outages continue, but it gives no clear picture of the outage trend or of what the coming weeks look like without the part.

qualification.reason: It sets a reply deadline (still a placeholder) and says the reply will be posted in the lobby, but it names no consequence if the deadline is missed and no checkable condition beyond that.

objections.reason: It takes on her likely objections directly: 'two out of every three households' answers the idea that this is a few loud people, and it deals with the passing certificate and the $400,000 answer without raising objections the facts already settle.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted open letter of roughly 430 words, close to the 400 asked for, and it works for posting in the lobby.
